approved: Introduced the companion Court Security (Consequential Amendments) Bill, which removes overlapping provisions from the 1971 Public Order Act to allow the new Court Security Bill's framework to operate cleanly across federal courts and tribunals.

Explained the Court Security Bill will replace the outdated Public Order Act with a modern framework giving trained security officers powers to search, screen and detain people at risk at Commonwealth courts including the Family Court of Western Australia and the Administrative Appeals Tribunal, with oversight from the Commonwealth Ombudsman.

Summed up the Court Security Bill, drawing on more than two decades practising family law to describe the stress, anger and hostility courts can see, and said the new powers for security and authorised court officers come with licensing, training and identification safeguards plus continued reliance on police for the most serious incidents.
